blocks.text: Expose a composer-oriented client contract: persisted draft state, transient composition state, attachment readiness, send, sequenced stream open or resume, idempotent Stop, retry, and authoritative turn snapshots. Keep raw transport parsing and history implementation outside view components.

A useChatComposer adapter returns the persisted draft, transient interaction state, current turn, and intent methods. send accepts finalized attachment IDs plus stable command and client message identities. The event contract resumes after the last accepted sequence and correlates every event with conversationId, streamId, messageId, and sequence.

Contract checks:
- Persisted draft, transient interaction, attachment readiness, current turn, Send, Stop, and retry form the composer surface.
- Stream events use one lowercase SSE protocol with conversationId, streamId, messageId, and sequence.
- Stable send and Stop command identities make lost-response retries idempotent.
- Resume continues after the last accepted sequence or falls back to an authoritative turn snapshot.
- Conversation-history loading remains outside this composer contract.

blocks.title: Contract checkpoint
blocks.text: A good API makes persisted draft ownership, transient IME state, attachment readiness, send and Stop command identity, stream resume, snapshot reconciliation, and retry visible while hiding raw SSE parsing.

send accepts text, finalized attachment IDs, command ID, client message ID, and AbortSignal at the client boundary. openEvents starts after the last accepted sequence so reconnects do not replay accepted deltas. Stop is an idempotent command: create one stopCommandId per user intent and reuse it after a lost response, while AbortSignal closes only local transport work. The UI uses resumed terminal events or getTurnSnapshot to reconcile authoritative message status after cancellation races.
